title: Hybrid cold-start detection and soft-pin thresholds for hardware profiles
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: Produce hardware-specific published profiles that incorporate transient cold-start and thermal effect signals and expose a conservative, tenant-aware 'soft-pin' threshold. This ticket implements the hybrid detection pipeline (local microbench + production sampling), defines the algorithm for soft-pin margin computation per model-version/hardware pair (A100/H100/L40S/MI300), and publishes profiles in the standard profile manifest format used by the runtime. Motivation: existing pinning is largely static and does not account for time-of-day thermal behavior or bursty cold-start patterns from multi-tenant workloads, leading to occasional SLA misses or overly conservative pins. Deliverables: data ingest pipeline for cold-start traces, soft-pin algorithm implementation, updated profile publisher that tags profiles with margin metadata and telemetry keys, documentation for operator usage, and a canary rollout plan.
tasks: Design hybrid measurement plan: define microbench suite (short prompt lengths, typical batch sizes) and production sampling hooks (edge-case slow tails)
Implement lightweight p99/p999 cold-start tracer in serving runtime and agent that samples first N requests per model-version per host
Aggregate telemetry pipeline: normalize traces across hardware SKU (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) and compute hourly distributions
Develop soft-pin margin calculator: inputs = baseline latency signature, cold-start tail delta, thermal variance factor, tenant SLO; output = recommended soft-pin delta and confidence score
Extend profile manifest schema with fields: soft_pin_margin_ms, confidence_score, observed_tail_window, telemetry_key
Profile publisher changes: sign manifests and push to profile registry with hardware tags and rollout constraints
Integration tests: simulate thermal drift and bursty traffic to verify automatic fallback and soft-pin adherence
Docs + runbook: operator steps to inspect soft-pin decisions, rollback pins, and interpret confidence_score
Canary rollout: 5% traffic to select hosts per region for two weeks, monitor p99/p999 and error budget
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema change merged and backwards-compatible (runtime accepts older manifests)
Telemetry pipeline emits hourly per-sku cold-start distributions with >=95% sampling coverage for test fleet
Soft-pin margin computed and published for at least one model-version on each target SKU (A100/H100/L40S/MI300)
Canary run shows no >5% regression in client-facing p99 latency and no increase in error rate attributable to pin changes
Operator can view per-model soft-pin rationale in Console and trigger an immediate revert
Corresponding docs and runbook published: Confluence link present in ticket
rollout_plan: Stage 2: publish initial profiles for low-risk models to canary fleet (5% traffic)
Stage 3: monitor 7 days, iterate on margin formula if >1% regressions in p99
Stage 4: broaden to 25% then 100% in region-by-region steps
Fallback: automatic revert to previous manifest if error budget exceeds threshold or confidence_score < 0.5
notes: 2025-02-12 - Initial scoping call with Runtime (Diego) and Telemetry (Liang). Agreed on hybrid approach: local microbench plus sparse prod sampling.
2025-02-14 - UX note from Product (Nora): Console should surface the confidence_score and a one-line rationale for each soft-pin to help incident triage.
2025-02-18 - Performance review: early microbench shows MI300 cold-start tail is less predictable under multi-tenant bursts; recommend wider confidence margin for MI300 initially.
2025-02-19 - Security: KMS signing of manifests is already in place; no extra keys required for this feature.

2025-02-20 - Decided to keep 'soft-pin' as advisory preference (runtime may still fall back when capacity constrained); follow-up ticket will explore strict hard-pin enforcement for enterprise customers.
